name: stanley-livingstone
_source: Project Gutenberg #5157 — How I Found Livingstone, by Henry M. Stanley (1872)

entries.title: Arrival at Zanzibar
anchors: On the morning of the 6th January, 1871, we were sailing through the\s+channel that separates the fruitful island of Zanzibar
Zanzibar from Africa\. The\s+high lands of the continent loomed like a lengthening shadow

entries.title: Setting Out from Bagamoyo
anchors: We left Bagamoyo the attraction of all the curious, with much eclat
defiled up a narrow lane shaded almost to twilight by the dense umbrage

entries.title: Across the Makata Plain
anchors: The long broad plain visible from the eminences crossed between the\s+Ungerengeri and Simbo was now before us, and became known to sorrowful
memory subsequently, as the Makata Valley

entries.title: Arrival at Unyanyembe
anchors: The signal sounded and the caravan was joyfully off with banners flying,\s+and trumpets and horns blaring
A short two and a half hours' march\s+brought us within sight of Kwikuru

entries.title: The War with Mirambo
anchors: Kwihara\. Friday, 11th August, 1871\.--Arrived to-day from Zimbili
I am quite disappointed and almost disheartened

entries.title: Through Ukawendi to Ujiji
anchors: We bade farewell to Mrera on the 17th of October, to continue our route\s+north-westward
All the men and I were firm friends now; all squabbling\s+had long ceased

entries.title: Dr. Livingstone, I Presume?
anchors: At last the sublime hour has arrived;--our dreams, our hopes, and\s+anticipations are now about to be realised
Our hearts and our\s+feelings are with our eyes, as we peer into the palms

entries.title: Cruise on the Tanganika
anchors: Had Livingstone and myself, after making up our minds to visit the\s+northern head of the Lake Tanganika
the absurd\s+demands or fears of a crew of Wajiji
